headline: Dealer plans US$3m farm-machinery service centre at Kara-Bulak; loan terms unpublished
dek: A Talasbank loan of about $2 million and a $1 million Rural Development Fund share would pay for 35 jobs and repair bays by spring sowing.
paragraphs: Alatau Agro Machinery LLC, the Talas dealer that has sold and serviced John Deere tractors and combines since 1995, announced on Saturday a US$3 million (IS 25.2 million at the official rate of 8.40) service and parts centre beside the Talas–Nurzhan road at Kara-Bulak, close to the Kara-Bulak Grain Logistics Depot. It is due to open before the 2027 spring sowing.

About $2 million of the cost is a Talasbank loan and about $1 million is co-financing from the Rural Development Fund, which reports to the Lieutenant Governor. The dealer puts in the land and its existing workshop on the site. IradOne reported the plan on Sunday, and the government said in a statement the same day that the centre would open before sowing.

The centre is to have repair bays, a parts warehouse and a mechanics' training room, and to take on about 35 staff. Neither the company nor the announcement said how many of those posts are new, what mechanics will be paid or how many machines the bays can handle at once.

Kanybek Zhorobekov, director of the Rural Development Fund, said the Fund's share is a co-financing grant tied to the training room and the parts stock. "Farms lose weeks every spring waiting for a part or a mechanic," he said. Melis Nurmatov, Minister of Agriculture and Water Resources, welcomed the project at the announcement. No state guarantee or subsidy beyond the Fund's share was mentioned.

The timing follows a record cotton harvest on the Fergana rim and a maize and potato glut in the Chu and Talas valleys, which has left many farms asking where a combine or tractor can be repaired before the next season. Dr Myktybek Abylov, an agronomist at Talas State University, said the weeks before sowing are the bottleneck. "A seeder that is not repaired by March is a field planted late, and a late field costs yield," he said. Until now, he said, many farms send machines to Nurzhan or wait for a visiting mechanic.

For members of the Kara-Bulak Agricultural Cooperative, whose grain store stands near the site, the distance matters. Chairman Kasym Tokon uulu said the cooperative's roughly 140 households run mostly older machines and would use a nearer workshop "if the hourly rate is something a household can pay". He said no one had yet told the cooperative what the rates would be.

That is the open question. The dealer's accounts are not published, and neither the company nor the bank has released the loan's term, interest rate or currency. Asked about the terms, Tilek Ibraev, the company's director, said they are "an agreement between the company and its bank". Talasbank had not replied to questions by deadline. The Fund's grant conditions have likewise not been published.

Farm output rose in volume but much less in value in the first nine months of the year, the Territorial Statistics Office has said, and new machines are priced in dollars while farm incomes are in som, whose street rate has drifted well above the official one. How many smallholders can buy the machines the centre will service, rather than only repair older ones, is not answered in the announcement.
The company said it expects to begin building this winter and to start recruiting mechanics after the new year.
